newsitem.title: USA: US financial, bank stocks hit hard in stock dip.
newsitem.headline: US financial, bank stocks hit hard in stock dip.

text.p: Financial and banking stocks were hit hard on Thursday after a potent report of December manufacturing activity raised fears that interest rates might be raised.
The December National Association of Purchasing Management's index came in at 54.0, jumping higher than forecasts of 52.3.
The report sparked a broad sell-off in stocks and bonds. Gold and retail stocks were also weak.

The Dow had more than halved early losses and was down about 38 points, or 0.58 percent, to 6410 in afternoon trading. The Standard & Poor's 500 Index was off by about the same amount on a percent basis, down 4.84 points to 735.9.

Small cap stocks, which had managed gains during a blue-chip sell-off on Tuesday, were faring even worse than larger companies. The Russell 2000 Index was off 1.12 percent or about four points to 358.55 and the Nasdaq was off nearly 10 points to 1281, or about 0.76 percent.
"The finance sector is taking it on the chin and retail stocks are getting hit pretty hard," said Paul Rabbitt, quantitative analysts Oppenheimer & Co.
The Standard & Poors Finance Index was off about twice as much as the Dow Industrials on a percent basis, losing 1.23 percent, or 1.01 points to 80.70.
J.P. Morgan & Co Inc shares dropped 3/4 to 96-7/8, Citicorp shares lost one to 102, Bankers Trust New York Corp slumped 1-1/2 to 84-3/4 and BankAmerica Corp shares fell 2-3/8 to 97-3/8.

Nervousness about crucial holiday sales hit retail stocks on Tuesday after J.C. Penney Co Inc warned of disappointing fourth-quarter earnings and thin profit margins in November and December. Its shares lost 1-3/8 to 47-3/8.
The forecast came after Dayton Hudson's statement that holiday sales were less than exciting and Nordstrom Inc warned of disappointing quarterly revenues.
Other retailers also fell. Sears, Roebuck and Co fell one to 45-1/8 and May Department Stores Co lost 7/8 to 45-7/8.
Computer retailers suffered after CompUSA Inc said same-store sales in December came in at half the levels forecast by Wall Street. Tandy Corp and Circuit City Stores also fell.
Gold stocks also suffered due to weakness in the price of gold, which touched three-year lows earlier this morning of $366.55 an ounce in London.

Standard & Poor's gold Index fell five points, or just over two percent, to 229.8. Newmont Mining Corp fell one to 43-3/4 and touched a new year low of 43-5/8. Barrick Gold fell 3/4 to 28 on the NYSE.
